%md
## Triage Service Requests with Select AI Agents

### The action workflow

A planner needs a controlled way to review the highest-urgency service request. This notebook creates two narrow database functions, registers them as tools, and runs an agent that may retrieve approved evidence and write one simulated planning-review record. It cannot change source service data or trigger an external workflow.

%md
## Activate the profile

Set `genai` as the active profile and limit its database context to the approved service view and simulated audit table.

%md
## Create the constrained database boundary

This is the learning step that makes the safety rule inspectable. The first helper only reads the highest-urgency request. The second can write one simulated `PLANNING_REVIEW` audit row, and checks whether that row already exists before inserting.

%md
## Test the read-only helper

Run the lookup yourself before registering a tool. It returns evidence but cannot write a row.

%script
SELECT state_local_get_priority_request() AS service_request_evidence FROM dual;

%md
## Reset prior agent objects safely

This removes only this notebook's team, task, agent, tools, and simulated audit rows. It does not change source business data.

%md
## Create tools, agent, task, and team

The tools are the agent's only abilities. The role and task explicitly prohibit source-data changes and external workflows.

%md
## Verify, run, audit, and prove idempotency

The final paragraph inventories the components, runs the agent, reviews the simulated action row and native history, then reruns the same request. The grouped count must remain one per request.

%md
## Conclusion

You built a constrained service-planning agent. It retrieves approved evidence and can write only one simulated planning-review record through an idempotent database function. Source business data and external workflows remain outside its authority.

name: Triage State and Local Government Service Requests with Select AI Agents
